who: two squad members sizing up a new recruit (a Duellist and a Brigand, or a Healer and a Guardsman)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So you're the new one. What can you do besides eat?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hold a line, lift a cart and keep my mouth shut. Mostly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two out of three will do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} picked you up in {town}? Off the guild bench?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Off the guild bench, out of debt. Same thing, these days.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you'll fit. Half of us owe someone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Duellist, they tell me. Show me your guard. No, the high one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll show you in the yard, not over a cup.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good answer. Proud ones who boast die first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another mouth, and the purse already thin. Lovely.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I was promised wages. Was that a lie?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not a lie. A hope. You'll learn the difference here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Welcome. The captain's fair, pays on time, and doesn't waste us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's more than my last master could say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep it that way and you'll sleep dry most nights.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fen-born? You've the boots for it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Born in the reeds, raised on eels and taxes nobody paid.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Reedwatch. Then you know outlaws by their first names.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stonepass lass. Which clan?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mine. Ask again when we've bled together.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair. Highlanders, eh? Warm as a smelter gone cold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You know what this crew's known for? Hangings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I heard. I came anyway. Hanged men don't rob you twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you're the right sort, or the worst.

who: squad members told to travel with the player (a Scout and a Guardsman)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We're on the road with {player} again. Pack light.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I always pack light. You're the one with three pots.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two pots. And you eat from both.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boots on before the cock's done shouting. Captain's orders.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The cock's got sense. He stays home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The cock gets eaten. Walk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Marching again, and still no coin since {town}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Keep walking. Grumble where the captain can hear it, if you're brave.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm not brave. I'm owed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wherever {player} goes, I'd follow. Even into the March.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You say that now. Wait till the Broken March smells you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I said follow. I didn't say gladly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Word is {band} hit the road ahead. We go anyway?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We go anyway. That's what we're for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then string the bows before the bend, not after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Leaving {town} hungry. Glad to see the back of it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hungry towns follow you. Every hamlet on the road will be begging.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we keep our bread inside our coats.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Travelling with a lord now. Do we walk behind, or beside?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Behind. Ten paces. With a spear, in case someone wants the title.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My lord {player} would laugh at that. Then do it.

who: squad members left to guard the player's hall (a Guardsman and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Guard {hall} while the captain's off having adventures.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Somebody has to mind the storehouse. Better us than the rats.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The rats don't get paid. Unlike us. In theory.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your watch. Wake me if the dogs bark twice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if they bark once?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then it's a fox. Let me sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Walls, walls, walls. I signed up to fight, not to count bricks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The last crew that got bored had their hall burned.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine. I'll count bricks. Angrily.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} hit a farmstead two hills over. They'll come here next.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them. Barracks is full and the gate's new.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Double the watch anyway. New gates burn as well as old.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Night passed quiet. Nobody tried the wall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Quiet nights are the ones raiders spend scouting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're a joy at breakfast, you know that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Captain trusts us with everything here. The stores, the lab, all of it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then nobody touches a sack while I'm standing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Spoken like a Guardsman. Sit, though. You'll stand all night.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our own walls. Never thought I'd guard something that wasn't a lord's.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is a lord's. Ours. Near enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then guard it like you'd hang for losing it.

who: squad members set to the hall's jobs at the forge, lab or stores (a Bladesmith and an Apothecary)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Forge duty again. My arms are bigger than my brains now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That was true before the forge.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pass the tongs, before I test them on you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This lab's no Little family stillroom, but the draughts come out clear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Keep it quiet. Stonepass doesn't like rivals brewing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then Stonepass can buy from us, and sulk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hauling sacks into the storehouse. A sellsword, carrying flour.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A sellsword eating flour, too. Carry it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd rather carry a spear. At least it fights back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Honest work. Warm forge, roof overhead. Could be worse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Could be a ditch on the Reedwatch road. I've slept in those.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So have I. This is better. Don't tell the captain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stores are full to the rafters. When did that happen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: When the captain stopped giving it away. Count the {good}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I count it. It counts higher every week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bank the forge. That's enough blades for one day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three good ones and one I'd sell to an enemy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sell it to {band}, then. Let them break it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stores are thin. If the captain doesn't trade soon, we'll eat the seed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then work faster. Blades sell when bread doesn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lean times make good smiths rich and good cooks sad.

who: squad members ordered out on missions (a Ranger and a Scholar)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Missions now. The captain wants us earning, not lounging.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Earning, or dying slower. Read the contract twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You read it. I'll carry the spears.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} has a board full of jobs. Which one's ours?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one with the most coin and the fewest teeth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Those don't exist. Pick the one with the fewest teeth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First mission under {player}'s banner. Let's make them proud.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's make them richer. Pride doesn't buy arrows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Both, then. I'm greedy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Out on missions while the captain counts coin at home.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain counts it because we bring it back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the captain can share it. Soon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Word's out a Blighted lair's leaking. That's our mission, isn't it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone has to go before the hamlets do the dying.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine. But I'm not touching the salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bags packed, maps rolled. Where's {site}, exactly?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Past the third beacon, then left where the grass goes grey.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Left at the grey grass. Lovely directions.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another ruin. The captain can't pass an old stone without poking it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Old stones pay. Libraries pay more. Hush and walk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd like a job that pays in bread, once.

who: squad members sent to clear a lair under a named leader (a Guardsman leading, a Scout following)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} says {B} leads this one. Don't look at me like that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fine. I lead. Where's {site}, and what's in it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something the guild won't touch. So, us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} put me in charge of this. I won't waste a one of you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Waste the beasts instead.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the plan. Shields first, bows behind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why are you in charge, {B}? I've cleared more barrows than you've seen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because I get paid the same and complain less.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine. But when it goes wrong, I'm saying so.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a Blighted lair. Nobody breathes the grey dust. Masks on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: These masks stink of vinegar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better vinegar than grey lungs. On.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We hit {site} at first light. Sleep now, if you can.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody sleeps the night before a lair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then lie still and pretend. It helps the others.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tracks. Big ones. The den's close.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wolf, or worse?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Worse walks on two legs. These are four. We're lucky.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Broken fort on the March. Stonepass wants it emptied.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stonepass wants everything emptied except its own purse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Their coin spends. Keep your shield up near the walls.

who: squad members back from a mission with loot (a Brigand and a Healer)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Back alive, and with a sack that clinks. Best kind of day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody limping. That's the part I'll remember.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You remember the limping. I'll remember the clinking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Drinks on the loot! First round, at least.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The loot is the captain's until it's split.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the captain buys the first round. Fair's fair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good haul. Now watch it vanish into the hall's walls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Walls keep raiders off our throats.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My throat would like a share first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {site} cleared. Tell {player} it was clean work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell them yourself. You did most of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We did it. That's what I'll say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: People already know about {site}. We passed a pedlar spreading it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Spreading it how? Did we kill ten or a hundred?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A hundred, by the time it reaches {town}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sun's going down and I'm still counting coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Count it twice. The captain will.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain counts it once and trusts us. That's worse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain'll want every penny of this, you know.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And will we see any of it? Last time we didn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep a coin back in your boot. Nobody checks boots.

who: squad members back from a mission without one of their own (a Guardsman and a Born survivor)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We came back short. {dead} didn't make it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I know. I was there. Don't say it again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone has to tell the captain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} died for a sack of rust and a few coins.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {dead} died for the wages we never got.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain will hear that. Today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It wasn't the captain's fault. The lair was worse than the guild said.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I know. I'm not blaming anyone. Just tired.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rest. I'll carry the bad news.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't sleep. Keep seeing {dead} go under.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You'll see it for a month. Then once a week. Then never.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's not comfort, you know.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Light a candle for {dead}. They'd laugh at it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They'd laugh, then light one for us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Light two, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We lost {dead} and came back to an empty granary.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: At least they don't have to go hungry now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a cruel thing to say. True, but cruel.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Brother at the chapel can say the words for {dead}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not Brother William. Anyone else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why not him?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sister Margaret wouldn't. That's reason enough.

who: squad members just paid on time (a Brigand and a Guardsman)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paid. On the day. I keep waiting for the trick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's no trick. Some captains just pay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then this one's rarer than an honest steward.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Coin in hand and a captain who earns it. Can't ask more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You could ask for more coin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I could. I won't. Not this week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wages in. Enough for boots and a drink.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Boots first. You'll want feet more than a headache.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Spoken like a mother.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paid at last. Took three weeks of grumbling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then stop grumbling. It worked.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It worked once. I'll keep my voice in practice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wages in the purse and {guild} round the corner.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Spend half. Send half home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half home, half here, and half for tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paid, but bread's a fortune in {town}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Coin's no use if there's nothing to buy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I'll buy someone's bread before they eat it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain keeps every promise, even to us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's why I stay. Not the coin. Well. Partly the coin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mostly the coin, and a bit the honour.

who: squad members whose wages were missed once (a Duellist and a Healer)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No coin this week. Did you get any?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not a penny. The captain says next week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Next week. Every lord says next week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wages late. Happens. Roads are bad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll wait once. Not twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Once is fair. Twice is a habit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Late again. My blade's worth more than promises.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A proud Duellist with an empty purse. Poetic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mock me, but you're hungry too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain's short this week. We'll manage.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I trust {player}. They'll make it right.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They always have. Tighten the belt one notch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No wages and lean times. Bread's dearer every day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I can heal a wound, not a belly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then pray the captain sells something soon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A lord with a hall, and we can't get paid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Halls cost more than sellswords. Ask any lord.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd rather not ask a lord anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shortage in {town}, and our wages caught it too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everyone's purse is light this season.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain's isn't. I've seen the storehouse.

who: squad members warning that they'll leave if not paid (a Brigand and a Guardsman)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tell the captain plain: pay us, or we walk.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll tell them. They won't like it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I don't like empty bellies. We're even.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My pack's ready. One more week, then I'm gone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give it a week. That's what we agreed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A week. Then the road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two weeks without pay. Next one, I'm off to the Grey Company.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Margaret Young doesn't take deserters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She takes the hungry. I'm hungry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd stay without pay, but my family can't eat loyalty.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then tell the captain that. They'll understand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Understanding won't feed them either.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half the camp's talking about leaving. You hear them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I hear them. I'm one of them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the captain has a week, not a month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: John Brokenose deserted Stonepass over wages. Now he's a king.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A king of a waste camp, waiting for a hero's blade.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better than unpaid. Tell the captain I said that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain's rich and we're not. Funny how that works.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not funny. Tell them: pay or we go.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Greedy captains learn fast when the barracks empty.

who: a squad member quitting over pay or the player's deeds, and one who stays (a Healer and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm going. Don't try to change my mind.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I wasn't going to. Take care on the roads.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And you. Watch the captain's back, since I won't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No coin in a month. I'm done.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where will you go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The guild. They pay in blood, but they pay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I won't march with someone who hangs farmers for spite.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They were helping outlaws.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They were feeding their children. I'm leaving.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain sold out those people for coin. I saw it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Coin keeps us fed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then eat it. I'll find a captain with a conscience.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sparing outlaws who'll cut our throats next week? I'm off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain thinks mercy wins more than steel.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mercy didn't save my brother. I'm gone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Too much praying, not enough fighting. I'm leaving.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The temple feeds us, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then let the temple fight the Crows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another ruin, another library. I signed on to fight, not read.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain finds things nobody else does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then let the captain find a new spearman.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain kept an oath to an outlaw. Paid for it in our blood.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A word's a word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A word won't bury me. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Packing, are you? Just like that?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Just like that. I've waited long enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Well. The road's long. Mind the Crows.

who: a wounded squad member resting and one tending them (a Healer and a Duellist)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lie still. If you tear the stitches again I'll sew your mouth next.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You're gentle as a bear, you know.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gentle bears lose patients. Lie still.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't sleep. The wound's on fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Drink this. It'll put you under till dawn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tastes like ditchwater.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it's working.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The infirmarian says a week. I say three days.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The infirmarian has buried more proud fools than you've met.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine. Four days.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wounded and unpaid. The captain can't even afford my bandages.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The bandages are free. I'm paying for them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you're the only one here worth anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good bed, warm broth. If I'd known, I'd have got stabbed sooner.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't joke. The next one might find your heart.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then it'll find it full of broth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tell the captain I'll be back on my feet before the next lair.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You'll be back when I say so. Not before.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Healers. Worse than sergeants.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a raid near {hamlet} and I'm flat on my back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let the others take it. You'll get your turn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I hate lying here while they fight.

who: squad members mourning one of their own (a Guardsman and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} is gone. Just like that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's how it always is. Just like that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll carve the name on the barracks post.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead}'s blanket is still on the floor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leave it a night. Then give it to someone cold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They'd want that. They were always cold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} gone, and for what? A captain who won't pay us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You're thinking of leaving.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm thinking I don't want to be next.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} died with the captain's colours on. That's something.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain will remember them. I'll make sure.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So will I. Every lair we clear, for {dead}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The priest says {dead} is with the saints now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The priest didn't know them. They'd be bored with saints.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then they'll teach the saints to play dice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We bury {dead} here, under the oak?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Under the oak. Facing home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which way is home? They never said.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then facing the road. They loved the road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Word of {dead}'s death reached {town} before we did.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pedlars. They carry grief faster than bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then their family already knows. Good. I couldn't tell them.

who: squad members after one has grown stronger or reached a new rank (a Gifted Duellist and a Born survivor)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you see that strike? I've never been that fast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I saw. You've got better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better? I've become the best in this squad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain made me a sergeant. Me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You've earned it. Don't let it go to your head.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Too late. It's already there, wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A drink for the new rank! On me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You've never paid for a drink in your life.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then this is a day to remember.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stronger, faster, and still paid the same.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ask for more, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I will. A sergeant's worth more than a spear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Practice. I want to keep this edge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Gifted ones always think they're done learning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm gifted, not stupid. Practice with me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Word's going round {town} that you're one of the best blades now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Let the Crows hear it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let the heroes hear it too. They get jealous.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thomas Fox had better watch his back. I'm coming for his name.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You'd want his job? Killing for Sir Robert?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. Just his name. And maybe his sword.

who: squad members given better arms or armour (a Guardsman and a Ranger)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New mail! Look, no holes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No holes yet. Give it a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're just jealous of my shine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain spent their own coin on this bow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then don't miss with it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I never miss. Well, rarely.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our own forge made this blade. Feel the balance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better than anything the guild sells.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better than Sir Robert's heroes carry, I'd wager.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New armour, but no wages. Can I eat a breastplate?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You can wear it while you starve.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I'll be the best-dressed corpse in {town}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stonepass steel. Sky iron in the edge, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They say that about every blade sold above the Wall.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This one's true. It sings when you strike it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Smiths are posting buy orders for ore. Steel's dear, and the captain still bought us swords.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the captain, spending on us before themselves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or spending so we don't leave. Either way, I'll take it.

who: a mage or healer squad member enrolled at the tower school by Mereworth, and a friend (a Scholar and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain's sending me to the tower school.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You'll come back with your nose in the air.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll come back with fire in my hands. That's better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paying my fees at Mereworth. The captain believes in me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then don't fail. That's a lot of coin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I won't. I'll learn everything they teach.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Coin for the tower school, and none for our wages?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not my choice. Talk to the captain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll talk. You go read your books.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another class graduated from the tower school. I'll be next.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You'll be the one who sets their sleeves alight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Once. That was once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Joan Thomson studied there, they say. Fire in her fingers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And look where it got her: married off for a treaty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm not getting married. I'm getting a staff.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Leaving for Mereworth today. Will you miss me?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll miss you mending my cuts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then try not to get cut till I'm back.

who: squad members looking at a newly finished part of the player's hall (a Mason and a Guardsman)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The barracks is finished. A real bed, under a real roof.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And a real wall around it. I'll sleep tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You sleep every night. You snore through raids.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look what {player} has built. This is ours now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ours to guard. Ours to die for, if it comes to that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's hope it doesn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Alchemy lab's done. The Little family won't like it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them sulk in Stonepass. We'll brew our own.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And sell it cheaper than theirs. That'll sting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A new storehouse. Built with our unpaid wages, I'd guess.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Built with your sweat, too. You carried half the stones.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll remind the captain of that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A hall worthy of a lord. My lord {player} has done well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lords' halls get raided by lords' rivals.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we'll need more walls.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A hall in Reedwatch. The Crows will see it from their camps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them see. Let them count the spears.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They count better than you think.

who: squad members during and after a raid on the player's hall (a Guardsman and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Raiders at the gate! Up, up!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Enough. Grab a spear and stop asking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They came over the wall in the dark. Where was the watch?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Asleep. Like everyone. Until the dogs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then from now on, two on the wall all night.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They took half the storehouse before we drove them off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half. Could have been all.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain won't see it that way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Raided again. And I'm the one who almost died, unpaid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You almost died for your bed. That's worth something.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My bed doesn't pay me either.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It was {band}. I saw their colours on the wall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They'll come back. They always do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then next time, we'll be waiting with pitch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They didn't get the barracks. We held.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain will be proud. Or furious about the stores.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Both. Captains always manage both.

who: squad members camping on the road at night (a Scout, a Brigand and a Healer)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fire low. No sense telling the whole road where we sleep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The whole road knows. Smell the stew.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then eat it fast, before someone comes asking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your watch. Two hours, then wake {B}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two hours of staring at dark trees.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stare harder. The trees around here have friends.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hear that? Wolves, off past the ridge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Far off. They've a deer tonight, not us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tonight. Keep the fire fed anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fen damp gets in your bones. Shift closer to the fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Closer and I'll be in it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you'll be dry, at least.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Desert's freezing at night. Who knew sand could be this cold?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every Sunward child knows. Burn the dung, not the blanket.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm not touching camel dung.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then freeze, fen boy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wind off the Wall would skin a goat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Highland wind. Builds character.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I've enough character. I'd like a roof.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You see that glow north? Like ash-light.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {calamity}. Men at the last inn said it rose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we sleep in our boots tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cold ground, thin stew, no wages. Living the dream.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You chose this. Nobody dragged you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The hunger dragged me. Same thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Captain's asleep. Let's keep it quiet, they've earned it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Aye. Took the first watch two nights running.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we take this one, and say nothing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The beacon on the ridge isn't lit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wardens get lazy. Or worse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Worse, out here, usually means the Blight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hamlet kids hanging round the fire edge again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give them the heel of the loaf.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And tomorrow we'll have none.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tomorrow we'll have the road. They won't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Captain's praying again, out there in the cold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them. Saints might be listening tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If they are, ask them for a dry blanket.

who: squad members after outlaws took their cargo on the road (a Caravaneer and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They took the cart. The whole bloody cart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They left us our necks. Count that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My neck doesn't sell for coin in {town}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It was {band}. Saw their marks on the arrows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we know whose camp to visit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With more spears than we had today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cargo gone, wages gone with it. Wonderful.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain will make it right. Somehow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Somehow isn't coin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Crows. Had to be Crows, this side of the fen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thornback only robs lords' seals. This was some other lot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Crow's a Crow to me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They were starving, captain. Half of them were boys.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Starving boys with sharp knives.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Still. I'd rather lose {good} than kill children.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We could catch them before dark. They're slow with the cart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Six of us, fifteen of them? We'd catch a grave.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we follow and wait for night.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jackals. Desert-thin and quick. Gone into the mesa by now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Saltcrown Mesa. That's where they cache it, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then someone should go look.

who: squad members arriving in a town together (a Duellist and a Healer)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {town} at last. Beds, beer, and someone else's cooking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Baths first. You smell like the road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The road smells like me. I'm older.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look at them. Ribs showing, all of them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Keep the bread out of sight. Hunger makes thieves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hunger makes us all thieves, sooner or later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {town}'s doing well. Market's full.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Prices are full too. Watch the purse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My purse is too thin to steal from.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hoods up. The gate guard's looking at us too long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain's face is on the notice board.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then walk faster, and smile less.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're cheering. For us. For the captain, really.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Enjoy it. Cheers turn quick in {town}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not today. Today I'm a hero's friend.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First Hearth. The old royal seat. Mind your manners.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Proud town. Everyone thinks they're a claimant.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half of them are, somewhere back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sunward. Count your coins now, they'll be gone by supper.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Taxes, tolls, then water. Everything costs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Even the air, I'd wager, if the Coin could bottle it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Canopy Rest. Smell the pine. And the incense.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Quiet town. Too quiet, some say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Quiet's good. Quiet means nobody's screaming.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stonepass. Keep your eyes down near the clansmen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They don't like lowlanders. Or anyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They like steel. We've got some to sell.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're shutting doors as we pass.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Word of the captain's deeds got here first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we buy what we need and leave by nightfall.

who: squad members eating together in camp or the hall (a Brigand, a Guardsman and a Cook)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pass the bread. No, the whole loaf.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You'll share like everyone else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm sharing it with my stomach.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rabbit again? Who caught this?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I did. Be grateful, it was slow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Slow rabbits are sick rabbits.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Roast pork and real ale. The captain's in a good mood.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or the stores are full. Same thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eat before it changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thin gruel, thinner every day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thin's better than nothing. Ask the hamlets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I know. I'm still allowed to hate it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's to the captain. To {player}!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: To {player}, and full bellies!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And to nobody dying this week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good stew. Shame we're paying for it ourselves.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain bought the meat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With our wages, I'd wager.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eels. Always eels in Reedwatch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eels are good. Eat up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They wriggle in my dreams, {B}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Black bread and mutton. Stonepass food.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hard food for hard people.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My teeth aren't that hard.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Porridge before the march. Eat it hot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's grey. Like the Blight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't say that at breakfast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Supper in our own hall. Feels like being a lord.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A lord doesn't wash his own bowls.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I'm half a lord. The eating half.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wait. The captain wants grace said.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The stew's going cold while the saints listen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Saints like their stew hot too. Be quick.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard {good}'s gone scarce in {town}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's why the cook's watering the ale.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm not watering it. It came that way.

who: squad members on a long march or in idle hours (a Duellist, a Brigand, a Healer or a Born survivor)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where were you born, anyway? You never say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A hamlet with more goats than people.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's half the realm.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How far to the next town?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Same as when you asked an hour ago, less an hour.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're a comfort, {B}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My grandfather fished these fens. Before the Crows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Before the Crows? There was a before?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Short one. Then the Steward Hall stopped judging, and the Crows came.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My sister married a guard of Sir Robert's.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then she married the throne's dogs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Say that louder in First Hearth. I'll watch you hang.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you miss home?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every day. But home doesn't pay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Neither does this. Often.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Crows are feuding again. Brothers fighting brothers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Leans and the Shortknives. Families never stop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mine never did either. That's why I left.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A hero broke a camp east of {town}. Clean work, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clean for the hero. Not for the camp.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You were an outlaw. I forget.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {calamity}. The name keeps getting longer every time someone says it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Names grow. Like fear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's hope the beast doesn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain's wandering off again to read some carving.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Old Steward marks. Everywhere, if you look.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who were the Stewards, really?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: People who lit fires nobody remembers why.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You ever think about the empty throne?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Never. Thrones are for lords. I'm for supper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone's going to sit in it. Better a good one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used to be a guildsman. Riftgate. Good pay.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then why leave?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half my party died in a rift. The guild sent flowers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You know the Forest Charter? Says poor folk can gather deadwood.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the lords' foresters hang them for it anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half Law. Half for us, half for them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When I was small, we ate nettles one winter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nettles aren't bad with salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We didn't have salt. That was the point.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you know Sister Margaret left Brother William's chapel?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Something about missing salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something smells wrong in that chapel.

who: an outsider (a townsperson, guard, merchant or outlaw) and a squad member

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You ride with {player}, don't you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I do. What's it to you?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Just curious. People talk about them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're with {player}'s lot. Need any {good}? Fair price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fair for you or fair for me?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair for the captain, who pays the bills.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your captain's wanted. Tell me where they sleep, there's coin in it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's a knife in it too, if you keep asking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No need to be like that. I'll go.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You march with {player}? Bless you all. My farm stands because of you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain did most of it. We just carried shields.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then bless your shields too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your captain's not welcome here. Neither are you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We're only buying bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buy it quick, then. Sergeant's watching.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is it true? {player} sits a hall now, like a lord?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: True. My lord {player}, now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Strange days, when guild boys become lords.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buy you a drink, friend? I hear {player} pays well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You hear wrong. Buy the drink anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ha. Fair enough. What's the captain really like?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stand where you are. Toll's a penny a head.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Count the heads first. Then count our spears.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On second thought, the road's free today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You march for the butcher who hanged them at {hamlet}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I march for coin. Not for hangings.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Same coin, though. Remember that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your captain spared my boy. He was with the {band}, but he's young.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain gives a second chance. Not a third.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He'll not need a third. I'll see to it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You there. Does your captain answer to {lord}, or to no one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: To no one. Ask them yourself if you like.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll tell {lord} what you said.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're {player}'s. Did they free the captives from the slavers' hold?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some. Not all. We tried.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My sister was there. Is she free?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Never heard of {player}. Should I have?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You will, soon enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everyone says that about their captain.

who: an outsider of the squad member's blood (outlaw, guildsman or rival hold) and the squad member

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Well, look at you. My own cousin, in a captain's colours.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And you in a band's rags. Mother would weep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mother's dead. She can't weep about either of us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thought I knew that face. You're a Shortknife, aren't you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Was. Now I'm one of {player}'s.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blood doesn't change with a new captain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your brother rides with {band} now. He asked after you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell him I'm well, and to stay out of my road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He'll be on your road whether you like it or not.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your uncle's a Lean. You know what that means in the Crows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It means trouble, everywhere I go.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It means protection, if you come home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sister! You're in the guild's tavern, wearing a sellsword's kit?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And you're the guild's best thief. We both chose our road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mine pays better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clan cousin. The Reavers took our farm. Are you with them now?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. With {player}. We'll get the farm back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I'll ride with you, if you'll have me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your captain hanged my brother. Your cousin, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I didn't know he was there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You'd have let it happen even if you did.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a price on your captain's head. I could collect it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You could. Then I'd collect yours. Family or not.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair. I'll not tell anyone you're here.

who: squad members approving something the player did (a Healer and a Guardsman)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That was well done. I'd not have thought of it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain thinks of things nobody else does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll follow that, gladly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain let them go. Gave them bread, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Kind. Maybe foolish, but kind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Kind wins more friends than fear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hanged the lot of them. No trial.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The roads will be quiet a month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain does what lords won't. I'll follow that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain kept the contract, even when it hurt.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A word's worth something with this one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rare enough. I'll keep my word to them, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cleansed the barrow and said the words over every grave.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The dead will rest now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So will I. Holy work's honest work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sold the {good} at twice the price. Clever.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clever, and we'll get our share.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain always pays. Greedy captains do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain found an old Steward inscription. Read it all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did it say?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something about fires. Light the fires.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We cleared {site}. The hamlets are safe a while.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain led from the front. Saw it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a captain worth following.

who: squad members disapproving of something the player did (a Healer and a Brigand)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I don't like what the captain did today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You don't have to like it. You have to follow it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll follow. But I won't forget.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Burned their hamlet to the ground. Children inside.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The captain says they fed the Crows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They fed their children. I'll not stay for the next one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sold the captives back to the slavers. For coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's good coin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I'll have none of it. That's blood coin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let the outlaws go. Again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They'll be back on the road by nightfall.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And cutting the throats of the people we're paid to guard.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another prayer, another candle. When do we fight?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Prayer and fighting can both be done, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not when the captain kneels while the Crows burn hamlets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We could have saved the hamlet. Instead we read old stones.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The stones may matter more. They talk of the Rim.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The hamlet mattered to the people in it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Kept faith with an outlaw contract over a lord's plea.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A contract's a contract.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a hanged village is a hanged village.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The captain spends our wages on lords and bribes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The bribes kept us out of the stocks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd rather sit in the stocks with coin in my boot.
